units.translation: On ⟦1⟧ cf. Homer Il. 9.593 ⟦2⟧, so Aeschylus ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ (fr. 239 ⟦5⟧, the Actaeon). Similar in overall thought are the choral song at vv. 368 ff., the chorus's antistrophe ⟦6⟧, 938–948. Blessing on agriculture, livestock, mining; cf. 905–908. ⟦7⟧ of storms that damage the trees (olives especially); ⟦8⟧ refers to the young plantings, which the storms do not harm, but which lose their buds through the fire; ⟦9⟧ however to the seed (⟦10⟧ 907). Whether ⟦11⟧ is the object of ⟦12⟧ (cf. ⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧), or (Dindorf) ⟦15⟧ means 'for my sake', makes no difference for the sense, but does matter somewhat for the construction in what follows, which has been damaged in transmission and which even the insertion of ⟦16⟧ does not fully remedy. But if one writes ⟦17⟧, then one can easily attach ⟦18⟧ to ⟦19⟧ (substantive) as a further elaboration. ⟦20⟧ of the eye of plants is a common metaphor (Theophrastus and others); on ⟦21⟧ cf. ⟦22⟧ 858 (292, 706, 1023); (⟦23⟧) ⟦24⟧ repetition of 479 (⟦25⟧) ⟦26⟧. The imperative is simply synonymous with the optative, cf. in the suppliants' blessing song ⟦27⟧ 669, 687, ⟦28⟧ 679. – The blessing of the herds is wished for ⟦29⟧ as follows: ⟦30⟧; similarly here ⟦31⟧. But the state of pregnancy must be followed by birth, and to this ⟦32⟧ clearly points; therefore ⟦33⟧, after which two syllables are missing, must be corrected in ⟦34⟧ with a missing infinitive, perhaps ⟦35⟧ (⟦36⟧). I do not doubt Dobree's ⟦37⟧ instead of ⟦38⟧: ⟦39⟧ ⟦40⟧; but ⟦41⟧ is always pejorative in Aeschylus. Now if because of ⟦42⟧ ⟦43⟧ was wrongly written instead of ⟦44⟧, then a following nominative has probably also been corrupted into the accusative: correctly ⟦45⟧ (⟦46⟧) ⟦47⟧, for which the Athenians are the object. How else is ⟦48⟧ to be explained? The reference to Laureion is clear in ⟦49⟧ and in ⟦50⟧, since Hermes is the god of lucky finds; ⟦51⟧ Aristotle ⟦52⟧. 19. 22, 7. Cf. ⟦53⟧.
and fire utterly destroys a city
dogs utterly destroyed the man, their master
I tell you the fortune of the murderous cauldron
and that the flame not pass its boundary
may the grazing flocks be prolific
may the gods' Hermaic gift honor
may the land-rich offspring honor the Hermaic gift
as the mines in Maroneia appeared
